Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing - follow-up and questions

Hi Lina,

Thanks again for the time today - really useful discussion. Quick recap and a few follow-up questions so we can finalize sizing and a pilot proposal: 

Summary of what I heard:
- Preferred deployment: Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool) - customer-managed data is not required; they want predictable throughput and SLOs.
- Target latency SLO: <=250ms p95 for text-generation API calls.
- Model class: leaning toward an LLM in the 13B-70B range (we discussed Llama-2-13B and a 33B variant).

Follow-up questions (to confirm so we size correctly):
1) Target TPS (requests/sec) at steady-state and at peak? Please include average requests per user if available.
2) Concurrency / session characteristics (how many concurrent users/threads at peak).
3) Token mix: average prompt tokens and average completion tokens (or sample percentiles).
4) Desired availability window (24x7 or business hours) and regional preference.
5) Any strict constraints on GPU type (H100 vs A100 family) or cost targets.

If you can send answers to the bullets above I'll run this through our capacity calculator and share an initial sizing + pricing workbook. I've attached a simple MAU/TPs worksheet and our latest Dedicated pricing deck for reference.

Next steps:
- You -> confirm the items above (1-5)
- Me -> send sizing options (cost + latency tradeoffs) within 48 hours

Thanks,

Rafael Mendes

Hi Rafael - thanks for the clear recap. Answers below: 

1) Target TPS:
- Steady-state: ~40 requests/sec
- Peak: ~120 requests/sec (short bursts up to 10-15 minutes)

2) Concurrency:~ we expect ~30-50 concurrent active sessions under steady-state, up to ~150 concurrent during marketing spikes.

3) Token mix:
- Avg prompt: 45 tokens
- Avg completion: 155 tokens
- So avg total ~200 tokens/request
- 95th percentile might be ~600 tokens/request for long responses (FAQ export flows)

4) Availability: 24x7, primary region: us-west.

5) GPU constraints: budget favors A100s but if H100 materially improves latency/cost we can consider it. Our procurement team will want a price delta.

Also - we have an internal goal of p95 latency <250ms for short queries (<=200 tokens) and are willing to accept higher latency for the long-tail (>=600 tokens).

Hope this helps. Happy to hop on a quick call if it's easier.

- Lina

Thanks Lina - this is perfect and very actionable. Based on your traffic profile (steady 40 TPS, peak 120 TPS bursts, avg ~200 tokens/request, p95 latency target 250ms for <=200 tokens) here are preliminary sizing options and tradeoffs: 

Option A - Performance (recommended for strict latency):
- GPUs: 4 x H100 (80GB) dedicated nodes
- Expected steady throughput: ~3200 tokens/sec aggregate (rough estimate; model dependent)
- Headroom for peaks and p95 SLO: should comfortably cover 120 reqs/sec bursts for the 13B model; gives capacity for growth and heavier completion percentiles.
- Pros: lowest latency, cleaner p95 margin.
- Cons: higher monthly cost vs A100.

Option B - Cost-optimized (if price-sensitive):
- GPUs: 6 x A100 (80GB) dedicated nodes
- Expected steady throughput: ~3000 tokens/sec aggregate (model and quantization dependent)
- Pros: lower per-GPU cost; good cost/token for sustained usage.
- Cons: slightly higher p95 latency under peak bursts vs H100.

Model notes: these estimates assume a quantized 13B-class model (we flagged 13B because you mentioned it explicitly); for a 33B or 70B class model we'd recommend adding ~2x GPU capacity and expect higher latency/cost.

Next steps I propose:
- I'll run these numbers through a more detailed capacity calc (include expected batch sizes, KV-cache hit assumptions, and regional placement) and share the workbook by EOD tomorrow.
- Marissa / Aditya - can you confirm whether we should price using A100 spot/reserved equivalents, or present both H100 reserved and A100 reserved options in the workbook? Also any standard overcommit policy we should apply to pilot offers?

Lina - once you sign off on the preferred option I'll coordinate a pilot month reserved config and provide a test window for performance validation.

Best,
Rafael
